messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: honeypot detected replayed session tokens to external IP 54.84.23.12 from auth-proxy-07. Pattern: repeating token reuse + POST /v1/sessions/validate. Count=310 in 8m. Pager: oncall-auth.
alice.w: oncall-auth here, joining. Can someone attach the raw honeypot capture? link to artifact?
bob.s: grabbing pcap + proxy logs now, uploading to secure bucket. s3://redwood-secure/evidence/1730001111/
charlie.sre: quick summary from honeypot: attacker replayed tokens that match format of our HMAC-signed session token (sid=hex + sig). Looks like token sig verified until we replayed, then failed later.
dana.support: customer-facing? any users impacted yet?
alice.w: early telemetry shows a small spike in 401s for web-login from the proxy cluster around the same time. No widespread account resets yet.
security-lead: tagging security@ for investigation. Initial suspicion: leaked signing key or token leak via a log forwarder. We need to assume token forgery risk until proven otherwise.
legal.liaison: looped in legal. If tokens map to PII or access records, we may need notification. Keep me posted.
bob.s: extracted minimal evidence: `proxy-log snippet: session=ab12cd... sig=ff34... remote=54.84.23.12` and honeypot request body included `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
ops-automation: running quick mitigation playbook: disable egress for proxy-07 and attach denylist for 54.84.23.12 across border routers.
charlie.sre: mitigation step 1: isolate node -> `kubectl cordon proxy-07 && kubectl drain proxy-07 --ignore-daemonsets`.
alice.w: agreed. Also enact temporary global reject for requests with header `X-Honeypot-Flag` to reduce noise from probes.
bob.s: push WAF rule to block requests with repeated reuse pattern. Doing now.
ops-automation: WAF rule applied: ID waf-rot-1730001111. Confirmed 54.84.23.12 blocked.
alice.w: next: rotate session signing key (HMAC). Plan: generate new key, issue short-lived fallback acceptance window, rotate tokens server-side, force reissue on next login. Need owner to run key rollout.
charlie.sre: I can run key rotation. Patch auth service to accept old key for 30m while issuing tokens with new key. Steps:
```
# generate key
openssl rand -hex 64 > /secrets/session_hmac_v2
# update k8s secret
kubectl create secret generic session-hmac --from-file=/secrets/session_hmac_v2 -n auth --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
# rollout auth deployment
kubectl rollout restart deployment/auth-service -n auth
```
bob.s: also plan HMAC verification in all validators to check both v1 and v2 during window. I'll prepare config change.
alice.w: timeline: rotate now, monitor 30m, then revoke old key and extend monitoring. Need coordination with support to handle forced reauths.
dana.support: prep status page snippet and API incident draft. Customers may see token expirations -> increased 401s. We should post advisory about temporary login refresh requirement.
security-lead: also collect and snapshot all config that references session keys. Search logs for exfil patterns: `grep -R "session_hmac" /var/log/` and check external sinks for accidental logging.
bob.s: found one pipeline config pushing debug proxy logs to a third-party CI (`ci-logger.prod`) with SSM role. Opening ticket to audit that pipeline.
legal.liaison: preserve evidence and restrict access to the secure bucket. We will escalate if PII is present. Please tag all artifacts with incident id 1730001111.
ops-automation: evidence staged at s3://redwood-secure/evidence/1730001111/ (access: security+legal only).
charlie.sre: rotation complete, new key deployed, auth pods restarted. Monitoring accepted tokens with new sig. Old key acceptance window set to 30m.
alice.w: good. Now run mass revoke for sessions created before `2026-03-17T10:00:00Z` as a precaution. Command:
```
python scripts/revoke_sessions.py --before 2026-03-17T10:00:00Z --dry-run
python scripts/revoke_sessions.py --before 2026-03-17T10:00:00Z
```
bob.s: dry-run shows ~1200 sessions to revoke. Schedule immediate job during low traffic window, but we should proceed given risk.
security-lead: proceed. Ensure rate limiting of revoke job to avoid overload.
dana.support: sending planned customer message now (internal draft): "We're investigating suspicious activity affecting session tokens; some users may be required to re-authenticate. No evidence of data exfil confirmed. We'll update in 1h." Publishing after legal approve.
legal.liaison: approve customer wording with minor edits. Hold notifications for 30m once rotation confirmed.
incident-bot: Incident 1730001111 state change: mitigation in progress -> keys rotated, node isolated, denylist applied. Paging: follow-up actions assigned.
bob.s: follow-ups: audit log-forwarding pipelines, revoke pipeline credentials, rotate any exposed CI/service tokens.
charlie.sre: forensics: capture memory snapshot of proxy-07 before we destroy it. `gcore` done, uploaded to evidence bucket.
alice.w: who is owning postmortem? Recommend oncall-auth + security-lead + ops.
security-lead: I'll own incident review. Assigning tosecurity+charlie.sre+alice.w.
alice.w: thanks. Next update in 30m or sooner if we detect further replays.
ops-automation: automation note: runbook step completed: `key-rotate -> revoke -> notify`. Logs: runbook/1730001111.log
dana.support: posted incident advisory to status page draft, waiting legal sign-off.
legal.liaison: signed off. Publish in 15m.
alice.w: closing realtime mitigation channel in 45m, moving to postmortem thread afterwards. Great work everyone. :+1:
